findings.text: The record says 'Two calls are exempt and named in the module' and names plasma_cell_trip_panels.py:406 and render_mechanism_evidence.py:510, but NON_RENDERER_CALLS in tests/renderer_wall_scan.py holds three entries, adding ('render_mechanism_evidence.py', 360). That third entry is load-bearing: I removed it in a scratch copy and the scan over benchmarks/ + docs/figures/ returns 81 records instead of 80, with render_mechanism_evidence.py:360 appearing - an unmasked draw_flux_contours of the analytic field. So the record's own account of its base count is internally inconsistent with the module it documents and omits a suppression it does not name; a reader reconstructing 80 from the record scores no way to reach it.

UnmaskedCall.path is set from self.path.name, so the record carries only the basename and drops the directory: the two extras in docs/figures/centroid-constrained-oracle-solve/repaired-remeasure{,-receipt}/measure.py both report as 'measure.py:70', and the several distinct render.py / measure.py / draw_trips.py files across the trees are likewise indistinguishable in the CLI output and in the test's site sets. The test absorbs this by asserting extras == {('measure.py',70)} against a separate +2 count, but a consumer of the printed records cannot locate a reported defect without re-scanning by hand.

test_reproduces_every_inventory_site asserts the scanner reports every one of the 78 reviewed defect sites by exact line, and test_base_count_is_inventory_plus_disclosed_drift pins the total at 80. This is a snapshot of a defect state rather than a regression guard: as the plan's repair followups fix these call sites the test fails by construction, and any unrelated line edit in a scanned file that shifts a flagged call re-pins the expectation silently. The guard the plan needs (report a NEW unguarded call) is not distinguished from the frozen 78-site inventory it also asserts.

The painter guard treats a call as wall-guarded only when the wall arrives as a keyword: 'any(keyword.arg == "wall" for keyword in node.keywords)'. nova/media/poloidal.py:147 declares wall as an ordinary positional parameter (wall=None, before **kwargs), so a call passing wall positionally - e.g. draw_flux_contours(ax, r, z, f, levels, style, color, lw, wall) - would be reported as unmasked when it is guarded. No such call exists in the reviewed corpus, so this is latent, not a present false positive.

The gate line reads '11 passed, zero added failures against base', but the reviewed run recorded no baseline arm: its manifest declares baseline_suite and after_suite empty and its logs contain only gate-renderer-wall-scan.log (a single 11-passed arm) and the negative control. The 'against base' clause is therefore not supported by the run's own records, though the substance holds - the after arm has zero failing tests, and my independent re-run at the reviewed head also passes 11 with EXIT=0.

gate_arms_note: The reviewed run declared no baseline_suite and no after_suite (both empty in its manifest), so added_failure_count is derived from the only gate arm it recorded: gate-renderer-wall-scan.log, revision bd9378109, command 'JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py', 11 passed EXIT=0, zero failing ids. added_failure_ids = [] and added_failure_count = 0. Independently reproduced by the review at the reviewed head in a scratch extraction: 11 passed EXIT=0 (review-gate.log). No baseline arm exists because the test file is added by 5abf0092a, so the 'against base' wording in the fragment (finding 5) is a record-accuracy defect, not a measurement error.

justifications.durability: The rule is pinned by a real, falsifiable test: the negative control reddens two tests when the wall guard is removed, and I reproduced that first-hand, so the guard demonstrably fires rather than merely passing. Weaknesses. The scanner is wired to nothing but its own test file - git grep finds no other importer and no pyproject/conftest/CI reference - so nothing but a manual pytest run exercises it. The test test_reproduces_every_inventory_site pins the current defect snapshot (78 exact sites by line) and test_base_count_is_inventory_plus_disclosed_drift pins 80; as the plan's repair nodes fix these call sites the test goes red by construction, so it is a change detector over a frozen defect count rather than a regression guard, and any line shift in a scanned file silently re-pins the result (finding 3).
justifications.evidence: The gate is recorded and reproduced: the reviewed run's gate-renderer-wall-scan.log shows 11 passed EXIT=0, and my independent run at the reviewed head in a scratch extraction gives 11 passed EXIT=0 (review-gate.log = /tmp/reckon-scratch/review-gate.log). The declared negative control (make the scanner accept a draw_flux_contours call without wall=) was independently reproduced by mutation: the two named tests fail (2 failed, 9 deselected, EXIT=1, review-negctrl2.log), the same signature the node's log carries. Deductions. (a) The record's gate line claims '11 passed, zero added failures against base', but the reviewed run's manifest declares no baseline_suite and no after_suite and its logs hold only the single gate arm and the negative control - so 'against base' is not substantiated by the run's own records, though added failures are genuinely zero (the after arm has no failures). (b) The fragment's allowlist account is internally inconsistent with the module it describes (finding 1): the count of 80 depends on a suppressed call at render_mechanism_evidence.py:360 that the record does not name, so a reader reconstructing the count from the record alone reaches 81.
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic: a single stdlib-ast module plus one test file, no new dependency, no new abstraction layer, no plan/sprint/ticket identifier in names, comments or the subject lines. It matches the read-only inventory-report idiom of the predecessor node. Deductions: the UnmaskedCall.path field stores only the basename (self.path.name), so records from different directories collide and the CLI cannot locate a site unambiguously - two distinct files report as measure.py:70, and the collision is what forces the +2 count reconciliation (finding 2); and the wall guard checks only the keyword form (keyword.arg == 'wall'), while draw_flux_contours accepts wall positionally before **kwargs, so a positional wall would be a false positive (finding 4, no such call exists in the corpus).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal - land a reusable source scanner that reports every wall-unmasked scattered-field renderer call over benchmarks/ and docs/figures/ and reproduces the 78-call inventory from the report-only predecessor - is met and independently reproduced. I extracted the reviewed head bd9378109 to a scratch tree and ran tests/renderer_wall_scan.py over benchmarks/ and docs/figures/: 80 records, and against the inventory literal in the test all 78 sites are present with extras exactly {('measure.py',70)} (two files sharing one basename/line, hence 78+2=80). The two extras were confirmed absent at the inventory revision a42dc665 (git cat-file -e fails on both paths) and present at head, each a draw_flux_contours call at line 70 - so the disclosed deviation is real and correctly attributed. Named controls behave as the record states: plasma_cell_fixed_point_attribution.py:424 and sol_ledger_current_census.py:415 are reported; render.py:52, plasma_cell_trip_panels.py:406 and contour_tree_explanatory_figure.py:359 are not; render_mechanism_evidence.py:510 is exempt while its siblings 511/516/868 are reported. Not full marks because the delivered evidence record understates its own allowlist (finding 1) and the scanner cannot locate a site unambiguously (finding 2).
justifications.scope_discipline: The review range 14f7a125f..bd9378109 touches exactly three paths - tests/renderer_wall_scan.py, tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py and docs/evidence/fragments/figure-and-solver-audit/fsa-renderer-wall-scanner.html - all inside the run's granted write paths. No renderer, product source, plan, shared index or concurrent-node path is touched (the node states 'no renderer edited' and the diff confirms it). Both commits carry a conventional subject and an explanatory body; a naming scan over the two source files returns no banned label, and neither commit message carries an AI trailer. The scanner is read-only: it performs no open()/write/mkdir/unlink, only ast parsing and printing. Deducted one only for the basename-only record key (finding 2), a design choice inside scope that degrades the record's usefulness.
